note: Prompt v2-vs-v3 comparison over an IDENTICAL 9-bundle set (ORS 328 + 332, tier=section, 7 reachable known candidates). NOTE ON NAMING: v2/v3 are PROMPT versions, not model versions. Every Gemma row is Gemma 4.

runs.caveat: 2 bundles unanswered; rates cover only the 7 answered.
Ran the FRONTIER SYSTEM_V3 (grading, worked examples); the local models ran LOCAL_SYSTEM/_V3. Model and prompt are confounded across that row.

runs.quote_lengths: median 222 chars, 1 of 8 under 40 — grounding is not gamed by trivially short quotes

runs.verdict: NOT VIABLE. Only 4 of 17 distinct document ids it emitted resolve to real documents even after case-folding: it invented ORS-070-063-0000, labelled OAR rules as ORS-, folded subsections into the id (ORS-328.331(4)), and emitted a literal '[Statutory reference]' placeholder. Also the slowest model tested despite being 3.8B, from thousands of reasoning tokens per bundle. phi4 x v3 was stopped partway and is not reported.

caveats: n=7 known candidates. Qwen's recall moving 1/7 -> 0/7 is ONE candidate and is not a signal; the grounding and phantom-id deltas rest on larger denominators.
Qwen scored 55% grounding here vs 28% on the earlier 50-bundle set, so these 9 bundles are easier. This is why the v2 control was run: the historical number could not have served as a baseline.
Recall-by-type scores against the HAND label, not the model's own `type` field, so a model mislabelling a type cannot change the recall number.
STILL NOT RUN: gemma4:12b x v3 — the 12B is the only local model that looked viable under v2 (14/14 grounding, 2/7 recall), and it has no v3 measurement. E2B fills the gap only at 2B scale.
Gemma 4 E2B x v3 produced 7 candidates, NONE matching a known one. High grounding means its QUOTES are real, not that the conflicts are. Those 7 are unreviewed.
Recall differences of 1/7 vs 0/7 recur across models and are ONE candidate each. Nothing here supports a claim that v3 changes recall in either direction.
finding: v3 consistently improves GROUNDING and citation discipline. Qwen 55%->90% with phantom ids 8->0; Gemma 4 E2B 33%->86%. Its effect on VOLUME is NOT consistent: Qwen fell 16->10 while Gemma 4 E2B rose 2->7. An earlier note here generalised 'v3 costs volume' from Qwen alone; E2B refutes that.
open_question: Whether the eight named types SUPPRESS findings: a model that cannot map what it sees onto one label may stay silent rather than mislabel. Haiku produced 1 candidate from 9 bundles, all of it correct. The narrows/broadens pair is provably ambiguous -- Haiku called the veterans-diploma rule 'narrows' (fewer qualify) where the hand label says 'broadens' (rule adds a requirement); both readings are right.
